Gm0KbW6Od30.title: Cable Russian twist
Gm0KbW6Od30.description: Lie on a stability ball and grab the handle with both hands. You should be approximately arms length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable. Draw the navel in and lift the hips to engage the glutes. Keeping the spine long , strong and straight, rotate your torso away from the pulley  allowing the hips to go through the natural intended range of motion.Pause as you complete a 90 degree turn then return to the starting position.

hPA98_r-6e4.title: Standing DB Calf Raises (Exercise Library)
hPA98_r-6e4.description:
How to do Standing DB Calf Raises:

Step-by-Step Instructions

Set-Up:

- Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms relaxed at your sides.
- Keep your feet hip-width apart and maintain a neutral spine.
- Optionally, stand on a raised surface (like a step or weight plate) with your heels hanging off for a greater range of motion.

Execution:

- Press through the balls of your feet to lift your heels as high as possible.
- Pause at the top and squeeze your calves.
- Lower your heels back down slowly to the starting position.
- Repeat for the desired number of reps.

Tips for Proper Form:

- Keep your knees straight but not locked.
- Avoid rocking or using momentum, stay balanced and controlled.
- Push evenly through both feet and focus on a full stretch and strong contraction.

Standing DB Calf Raise Key Benefits

- Builds size and strength in the calves for better athletic performance and lower-body balance.
- Improves ankle stability and foot control.
- Easy to perform with minimal equipment and setup.

tb7JtugjLQ8.title: Band Good Morning Pull Through, Tutorial, Exercise Video, Workout, SEXioFIT
tb7JtugjLQ8.description:
Type: Powerlifting
Main Muscle Worked: Hamstrings
Other Muscles: Glutes, Lower Back
Equipment: Bands
Mechanics Type: Compound
Level: Beginner

a) For this exercise you will need to tie one end of the band to something heavy and strong, like a post. Put the other end of the band around your neck.
b) Lower your upper body to form a 90-degree angle with both of your legs slanted a bit.
c) This will be your starting position. Use your strength to try to stand up again. When your body is straight, stay in this position for a couple of seconds and then, return to your starting position.
d) Repeat this exercise as much as you can.
